source.title: Exploring the Relationship between In-Context Learning and Instruction Tuning
source.authors: Han-Yu Duan; Yixuan Tang; Yi Yang; Ahmed Abbasi; K. Tam

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures similarity between hidden states from different inference/training conditions within the same LLaMA-2 model. It does not test convergence between independently trained models or any of the listed claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper's empirical results concern whether in-context learning (ICL) and instruction tuning (IT) produce similar hidden states within one model. That is related to representation similarity but is not the cross-model convergence named by the claim versions. The paper also reports prediction accuracy and per-token loss results; these do not measure the listed representation-convergence claims and are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study compares last-token hidden states of one LLaMA-2 model under zero-shot, in-context learning and LoRA instruction tuning (same base weights). It does not compare independently trained models, seeds, modalities, cross-model maps or shared features, so none of V1-V7 is tested. It does not cite the original sources, and it does not use convergence as a tool. 'Convergence' here means ICL and IT states of the same model being similar, a different construct.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct in substance. The authors conclude that 'ICL is implicit IT': ICL changes hidden states as if the demonstrations had been used to tune the model. They add that this convergence depends on demonstration properties (similarity, number, labels) and on instructions. They report it holds for LLaMA-2-13B and for machine translation.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares ICL and instruction tuning, not the original sources' cross-model convergence methods.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported within-model ICL-IT similarity varies with demonstration-inference semantic similarity, number of demonstrations, label correctness, task, layer, model size, and whether instructions are used in tuning.

fits_no_version.finding: In LLaMA-2-7B, final-layer last-token states under ICL and under IT are highly similar (~0.9), while each has near-zero similarity to the zero-shot anchor.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Within one LLM, in-context demonstrations and instruction tuning on the same demonstrations move the hidden state to similar points.

fits_no_version.finding: ICL-IT similarity rises with demonstration-inference semantic similarity (~0.4 to ~0.8) and with shot count. Wrong labels slightly lower it and increase its variance. Supervised tuning without instructions gives lower ICL-SL similarity. Across layers the similarity is U-shaped.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Within-model ICL-IT hidden-state convergence depends on the demonstrations, the presence of instructions, and the layer.

record.code_released: not stated; the paper says experimental codes will be made available for replication.
record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: The main evidence is similarity between ICL and IT states within the same model, so it does not establish cross-model convergence. Most results are presented in figures without numerical values in the text. The reported experiments use LLaMA-2 7B and 13B and the described sentiment and translation tasks.
record.rows_left_out: The paper reports prediction-accuracy comparisons for wrong versus correct demonstration labels and per-token loss decreases from instruction tuning, but these do not measure the representation-convergence versions in the claim. Individual plotted values at each of the 10 semantic-similarity levels, each shot-count value, and each layer are not transcribed separately; the rows record the text-described trends and layer pattern.

untested.parts: No cross-model comparison of independently trained models or alignment trend with scale. The 7B vs 13B result compares within-model ICL/IT states, not cross-model alignment.
No comparison of same-architecture networks trained from different initializations. The 30 seeds only randomize the sampled instruction, demonstration and inference example.
No mapping or stitching between models.
No cross-model feature or circuit analysis.
Uses an unspecified similarity measure on within-model states only. It reports no metric dependence of cross-model convergence.
No cross-model alignment measured, so neither incompleteness nor its causes are tested.

record.verdict_notes: The relation is changed from 'discusses' to 'cites_only' (T6): the paper neither discusses nor cites the cross-model representation-convergence literature. The overlap is only in the word 'convergence'. R7-R10 are marked 'partial' only because each is one point of a rising trend; since they link to no version, state is moot. The similarity measure is never named in the text (presumably cosine).

versions.untested_parts: Does not compare representations of independently trained models with different architectures, objectives or data, or test whether their alignment rises with scale and capability.
Does not compare vision and language model representations of paired images and captions.
Does not compare networks with the same architecture trained from different initializations or measure shared features or subspaces.
Does not map representations between different models, stitch layers, use relative representations, or test unpaired mapping.
Does not test whether interpretable features or circuits recur across models.
Does not test the dependence of cross-model convergence on similarity metrics, metric settings, or input distributions.
Does not test whether cross-model alignment is incomplete or attributable to shared training data or objectives.

relation.reason: The paper discusses a related within-model convergence construct; the text supplies no citation of the catalog's cross-model convergence claim.

tranche.reason: The study measures ICL–IT hidden-state similarity using the same base weights. It neither tests nor uses V1–V7.

source_check.notes: All rows correctly have versions=none; their measures cannot determine V1–V7, so observed/partial states should be cannot_determine. The authors' conclusion is accurately paraphrased; no synthesis statements or verdict labels are listed.
